```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
davisdata <- read.csv(file="UCDavis.csv")
data = davisdata
```
 Our Goal is to answer this question Is there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row
 you choose to sit in??

# Introduction  
The question is this: Is there a relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink?  
Data is from Uc Davis Math 116 class.  
$H_0$ There is no relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink.   
$H_A$ There is a relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink.  


# Methods 
Seat is a categorical variable.   
Alcohol is a numerical variable. 



# Data Summaries. 


## Now add in boxplot

```{r}
boxplot(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```
    
    
  The plot show that students who sit in the back tend to drink more oz/per week of alcohol than students who sit in the front or in the middle of the class.  
  
  
  

## Numerical Summaries

```{r}
favstats(alcohol~Seat,data=ucdavis1)
```


The numerical summary show that the students who sit in the back of the class drink 7 times more oz/per week of alcohol than the students in the front and middle who drink 2 - 4 oz/per week. 
## Inferential Tests

```{r}
model1 <- aov(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
summary.aov(model1)
```

The P value is 0.000116 which is less than 0.05, we fail to reject the $H_o$, we conclude that there is a relationship between where students sit and how much oz/per week of alchol is consumed.  

```{r}
plot(TukeyHSD(model1))
```

  The Tuckey graph shows there is a difference of alcohol consumptions between students who sit in the front and back,  middle and back, and there is no difference between the students who sit in the front and middle. 

## Conclusions
The question was: was there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row you choose to sit in.

Based on the Anova, and the Tukey plot comparing the means of seating positions: front, middle, and back and their alcohol consumption. I found that there is a difference in alcohol intake per oz/per week and the class seating arrangement. This is supported by the graphical and numerical results. There is a difference between the students who sit in the front and back, and also the middle and back, but there is no clear difference between the students who sit in the middle and front.
